answer: Practically, the chain should require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because falcon only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, canyon is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any ferrous approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
